description: Storage, LevelDB and chainstate persistence health: volume capacity, per-database read/write latency and hit rate, chainstate flush cost and triggers, block file I/O, pruning, snapshots and optional indexes. The layer every chainstate stall is attributable to.

panels.description: Used and free space on the data volume: about 933 GB used against 181 GB free, so utilisation sits near 84%. The two lines are mirror images, so watch the gap closing rather than the absolute level of either. Capacity lives here rather than on System Metrics because running out of space aborts the chainstate flush.
panels.title: Volume Usage

panels.description: Filesystem utilisation, about 84%. The chainstate flush path checks available space before every write and refuses once it is exhausted, so this is the panel that predicts a fatal disk-space abort.
panels.title: Volume Used Percent

panels.description: Mean LevelDB read latency per database. chainstate serves the coins cache, index the block index, and txindex the optional transaction index. Reads here are the ones that missed the cache, so this is the number to watch when a chainstate stall needs explaining. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Read Latency by Database

panels.description: Fraction of reads served without touching disk, per database. A falling rate means the working set has outgrown the block cache and reads are going to the table files. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Read Hit Rate by Database

panels.description: Mean time to commit a write batch, per database. A rising value here means the write path is becoming the bottleneck rather than read latency. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Write Batch Latency

panels.description: Write batches per second against explicit sync writes. Sync writes force a flush to stable storage and are far more expensive, so a sync-write spike explains a latency spike. Read failures should sit at zero. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Write Batches & Sync Writes

panels.description: Time to flush the chainstate to disk. This is the main chainstate I/O cost and was only visible in bench logs before instrumentation. Periodic writes should be fast; a FORCE_SYNC during shutdown is legitimately slow. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Flush Duration

panels.description: Which condition triggered each flush. PERIODIC is routine background writing, IF_NEEDED means the cache exceeded its share, and FORCE_SYNC is an emergency or shutdown write. The mix tells you whether flushes are routine or forced. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Flush Trigger

panels.description: Number of coins written on the last flush against the dirty count that triggered it. Flush duration scales with this, so read the two panels together. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Coins Written per Flush

panels.description: Dynamic memory held by the coins cache when the chainstate was last flushed. This is the input to flush cost: a large dirty cache is what makes a periodic write take as long as it does. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Coins Cache Memory at Flush

panels.description: Block file throughput as blocks are read and written. Reads dominate during initial sync and during any reorg replay; writes track new blocks only. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Block Read & Write Throughput

panels.description: Mean time to read or write a block file. Rising write latency with flat throughput points at the storage device rather than at load. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Block Read & Write Latency

panels.description: Latency of writing the block index and the undo data. The undo file is written for every connected block and is what makes a reorg possible without re-downloading. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Index & Undo Write Latency

panels.description: Block file read and write failures, including checksum mismatches. Any non-zero value here means disk corruption or a failing device, not a transient error. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Block File Failures

panels.description: Index entries and block files touched per second, plus undo bytes written. Undo bytes scale with how many inputs the block spends, so a large block shows up here. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Index Write Volume

panels.description: Block files actually deleted per second, against the number eligible for pruning. All zero on an unpruned node, which is the normal configuration. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Pruning Activity

panels.description: Cost of deciding what to prune and then unlinking it. Both read only block index metadata, not block data. Manual is the explicit -pruneblockchain call. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Prune Scan Cost

panels.description: Time to flush an assumeutxo snapshot to disk. Only active while a snapshot is being loaded or validated, so a flat zero line is expected on a node that never does. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Snapshot Flush

panels.description: Cost of recomputing UTXO statistics during snapshot validation, plus the abort rate. An abort means the snapshot did not match the assumed chain state. The abort counter is a count sharing a microsecond axis, so read it from the legend rather than the plot height. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Snapshot Stats & Aborts

panels.description: Block height each optional index has reached. A persistent gap behind the chain tip (see the Blocks dashboard) means an index is still syncing or has stalled, which silently disables the RPCs that depend on it. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Index Sync Progress

panels.description: Per-block indexing cost against reorg rewind activity. A rewind means an index had to roll back because the chain reorganised, which is normal but should be rare. The rewind counter shares the microsecond axis only for context. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Index Block Cost & Reorg Rewinds
